subject.title: Agent confabulates completed actions on Telegram surface — same config works reliably on Claude Code/Codex

question: Should OpenClaw add core action-claim verification or fail-closed semantics for Telegram/ACP turns beyond the existing private-final warning and message_tool_only delivery contract?
rationale: The fix changes whether final assistant text is private, rejected, revised, or delivered when it claims side effects without matching tool evidence, which is a product and privacy boundary rather than a mechanical bug patch.

options.title: Define core verification policy
options.body: Specify which claimed actions must be backed by observed tool completions, then implement a bounded verifier/revision path with live Telegram and ACP proof.

options.title: Limit to diagnostics first
options.body: Keep delivery semantics unchanged and add richer live repro instrumentation before choosing fail-closed behavior.

options.title: Fold into narrower delivery issues
options.body: Treat arbitrary action claims as out of scope for now and let #85714/#99536 handle only stranded message-tool final replies.

recommendation.title: Define core verification policy
recommendation.body: Specify which claimed actions must be backed by observed tool completions, then implement a bounded verifier/revision path with live Telegram and ACP proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses ACP/native hook behavior and product policy, where steipete has recent adjacent history and was mentioned in the issue timeline.
